original_question: List the card names with value that cost more converted mana for the face.
original_evidence: more converted mana for the face refers to Max(faceConvertedManaCost);
previous_SQLite: SELECT name FROM cards ORDER BY faceConvertedManaCost LIMIT 1
accepted_SQLite: SELECT DISTINCT name FROM cards WHERE faceConvertedManaCost = (SELECT MAX(faceConvertedManaCost) FROM cards)
review_basis: Fix ascending minimum selection; retain original evidence MAX(faceConvertedManaCost), rather than adopt the revised ConvertedManaCost task. Return all distinct maximum-cost names.

original_question: Please list the Italian names of the cards in the set Coldsnap with the highest converted mana cost.
original_evidence: card set Coldsnap refers to name = 'Coldsnap'; Italian refers to language = 'Italian'; highest converted mana cost refers to MAX(convertedManaCost)
previous_SQLite: SELECT T2.name FROM foreign_data AS T1 INNER JOIN cards AS T2 ON T2.uuid = T1.uuid INNER JOIN sets AS T3 ON T3.code = T2.setCode WHERE T3.name = 'Coldsnap' AND T1.language = 'Italian' ORDER BY T2.convertedManaCost DESC
accepted_SQLite: WITH eligible AS (SELECT f.name AS italian_name,c.convertedManaCost AS cost FROM foreign_data f JOIN cards c ON c.uuid=f.uuid JOIN sets s ON s.code=c.setCode WHERE s.name='Coldsnap' AND f.language='Italian') SELECT DISTINCT italian_name FROM eligible WHERE cost=(SELECT MAX(cost) FROM eligible)
review_basis: Italian names are foreign_data.name, not cards.name; keep all distinct names tied for maximum cost within the eligible Italian/Coldsnap set.

original_question: In duels, what are the top 10 cards with the highest uncoverted mana cost?
original_evidence: duels refer to format = 'duel'; the highest uncoverted mana cost refers to MAX(manaCost)
previous_SQLite: SELECT DISTINCT name FROM cards WHERE uuid IN ( SELECT uuid FROM legalities WHERE format = 'duel' ) ORDER BY manaCost DESC LIMIT 0, 10
accepted_SQLite: SELECT c.name FROM cards c WHERE c.uuid IN (SELECT l.uuid FROM legalities l WHERE l.format='duel') GROUP BY c.name ORDER BY MAX(c.manaCost) DESC LIMIT 10
review_basis: Keep original unconverted manaCost. Explicit maximum eligible manaCost per distinct name resolves DISTINCT/nonprojected ordering. No extra tie-breaking key is required.

original_question: How many posts were created on 21st July, 2010?
original_evidence: created on 21st July, 2010 refers to CreationDate BETWEEN '2010-07-21 00:00:00' and '2012-07-21 23:59:59';
previous_SQLite: SELECT COUNT(id) FROM postHistory WHERE date(CreationDate) = '2010-07-21'
accepted_SQLite: SELECT COUNT(Id) FROM posts WHERE date(CreaionDate)='2010-07-21'
review_basis: The question counts created posts; postHistory includes edits and repeated events and is not the posts entity. Use the shipped schema spelling posts.CreaionDate, verified from PRAGMA table_info.

original_question: Name the top 3 drivers and the points they scored in the 2017 Chinese Grand Prix.
previous_SQLite: SELECT T3.forename, T3.surname, T2.points FROM races AS T1 INNER JOIN driverStandings AS T2 ON T2.raceId = T1.raceId INNER JOIN drivers AS T3 ON T3.driverId = T2.driverId WHERE T1.name = 'Chinese Grand Prix' AND T1.year = 2017 ORDER BY T2.points DESC LIMIT 3
accepted_SQLite: SELECT d.forename,d.surname,s.points FROM races r JOIN results s ON s.raceId=r.raceId JOIN drivers d ON d.driverId=s.driverId WHERE r.name='Chinese Grand Prix' AND r.year=2017 ORDER BY s.positionOrder LIMIT 3
review_basis: Use the individual race results/finishing order and race points, rather than season-to-date driverStandings.

original_question: List down top 3 German drivers who has the shortest average pit stop duration and were born between 1980-1985.
original_evidence: Full name of the driver refers to drivers.forename and drivers.surname; born between 1980-1985 refers to 1980< year(dob)>1985; Average pitstop duration refers to Divide(SUM(duration),COUNT(duration)); shortest average refers to Min(avg(duration));
previous_SQLite: SELECT T2.forename, T2.surname FROM pitStops AS T1 INNER JOIN drivers AS T2 on T1.driverId = T2.driverId WHERE T2.nationality = 'German' AND STRFTIME('%Y', T2.dob) BETWEEN '1980' AND '1985' GROUP BY T2.forename, T2.surname ORDER BY AVG(T1.duration) LIMIT 3
accepted_SQLite: SELECT T2.forename, T2.surname FROM pitStops AS T1 INNER JOIN drivers AS T2 ON T1.driverId = T2.driverId WHERE T2.nationality = 'German' AND STRFTIME('%Y', T2.dob) BETWEEN '1980' AND '1985' GROUP BY T2.forename, T2.surname ORDER BY AVG(T1.milliseconds) LIMIT 3
review_basis: Use numeric pit-stop milliseconds instead of AVG(duration text), preserving original nationality/year predicates and name projection/grouping.

original_question: Among all the lap records set on various circuits, what is the time for the fastest one?
previous_SQLite: SELECT time FROM lapTimes ORDER BY (CASE WHEN INSTR(time, ':') <> INSTR(SUBSTR(time, INSTR(time, ':') + 1), ':') + INSTR(time, ':') THEN CAST(SUBSTR(time, 1, INSTR(time, ':') - 1) AS REAL) * 3600 ELSE 0 END) + (CAST(SUBSTR(time, INSTR(time, ':') - 2 * (INSTR(time, ':') = INSTR(SUBSTR(time, INSTR(time, ':') + 1), ':') + INSTR(time, ':')), INSTR(time, ':') - 1) AS REAL) * 60) + (CAST(SUBSTR(time, INSTR(time, ':') + 1, INSTR(time, '.') - INSTR(time, ':') - 1) AS REAL)) + (CAST(SUBSTR(time, INSTR(time, '.') + 1) AS REAL) / 1000) ASC LIMIT 1
accepted_SQLite: SELECT time FROM lapTimes ORDER BY milliseconds ASC LIMIT 1
review_basis: Rank stored numeric milliseconds instead of the incorrect textual-time parser; preserve original one-column, Top-1 output without added joins/tie breakers.

original_question: Which top 20 driver created the shortest lap time ever record in a Formula_1 race? Please give them full names.
original_evidence: shortest lap time refers to MIN(time); the time format for the shortest lap time is 'MM:SS.mmm' or 'M:SS.mmm'; full name of the driver refers to forename, surname
previous_SQLite: WITH lap_times_in_seconds AS (SELECT driverId, (CASE WHEN SUBSTR(time, 1, INSTR(time, ':') - 1) <> '' THEN CAST(SUBSTR(time, 1, INSTR(time, ':') - 1) AS REAL) * 60 ELSE 0 END + CASE WHEN SUBSTR(time, INSTR(time, ':') + 1, INSTR(time, '.') - INSTR(time, ':') - 1) <> '' THEN CAST(SUBSTR(time, INSTR(time, ':') + 1, INSTR(time, '.') - INSTR(time, ':') - 1) AS REAL) ELSE 0 END + CASE WHEN SUBSTR(time, INSTR(time, '.') + 1) <> '' THEN CAST(SUBSTR(time, INSTR(time, '.') + 1) AS REAL) / 1000 ELSE 0 END) AS time_in_seconds FROM lapTimes) SELECT T2.forename, T2.surname, T1.driverId FROM (SELECT driverId, MIN(time_in_seconds) AS min_time_in_seconds FROM lap_times_in_seconds GROUP BY driverId) AS T1 INNER JOIN drivers AS T2 ON T1.driverId = T2.driverId ORDER BY T1.min_time_in_seconds ASC LIMIT 20
accepted_SQLite: SELECT d.forename,d.surname,d.driverId FROM drivers d JOIN (SELECT driverId,MIN(milliseconds) AS fastest FROM lapTimes GROUP BY driverId) t ON t.driverId=d.driverId ORDER BY t.fastest ASC LIMIT 20
review_basis: Rank each driver by minimum native milliseconds. This answers fastest laps without SQLite substring/coercion dependence or Oracle empty-string comparisons. Retain the historical three-column output contract.

original_question: Who are the top 5 players who perform better in crossing actions? Indicate their player id.
original_evidence: perform better in crossing actions refers to MAX(crossing)
previous_SQLite: SELECT id FROM Player_Attributes ORDER BY crossing DESC LIMIT 5
accepted_SQLite:
SELECT player_api_id
FROM Player_Attributes
GROUP BY player_api_id
ORDER BY MAX(crossing) DESC, player_api_id ASC
LIMIT 5;
review_basis: Official correction returns player_api_id and ranks MAX(crossing) per player, with player_api_id as an explicit tie breaker.

original_question: Indicate the full names of the top 10 players with the highest number of penalties.
original_evidence: full name refers to player_name; players with highest number of penalties refers to MAX(penalties);
previous_SQLite: SELECT t2.player_name FROM Player_Attributes AS t1 INNER JOIN Player AS t2 ON t1.id = t2.id ORDER BY t1.penalties DESC LIMIT 10
accepted_SQLite:
SELECT t2.player_name
FROM Player_Attributes AS t1
JOIN Player AS t2 ON t1.player_api_id = t2.player_api_id
GROUP BY t2.player_api_id, t2.player_name
ORDER BY MAX(t1.penalties) DESC, t2.player_api_id ASC
LIMIT 10;
review_basis: Official correction joins player_api_id and ranks each distinct player by MAX(penalties), with player_api_id tie breaking.

original_question: For the teams with normal build-up play dribbling class in 2014, List the names of the teams with less than average chance creation passing, in descending order of chance creation passing.
original_evidence: normal build-up play dribbling class refers to buildUpPlayDribblingClass = 'Normal'; in 2014 refers to date > = '2014-01-01 00:00:00' AND date < = '2014-01-31 00:00:00'; names of the teams refers to team_long_name; less than average chance creation passing = DIVIDE(SUM(chanceCreationPassing), COUNT(id)) > chanceCreationPassing;
previous_SQLite: SELECT t3.team_long_name FROM Team AS t3 INNER JOIN Team_Attributes AS t4 ON t3.team_api_id = t4.team_api_id WHERE t4.buildUpPlayDribblingClass = 'Normal' AND t4.chanceCreationPassing < ( SELECT CAST(SUM(t2.chanceCreationPassing) AS REAL) / COUNT(t1.id) FROM Team AS t1 INNER JOIN Team_Attributes AS t2 ON t1.team_api_id = t2.team_api_id WHERE t2.buildUpPlayDribblingClass = 'Normal' AND SUBSTR(t2.`date`, 1, 4) = '2014') ORDER BY t4.chanceCreationPassing DESC
accepted_SQLite: SELECT t.team_long_name FROM Team t JOIN Team_Attributes a ON t.team_api_id=a.team_api_id WHERE a.buildUpPlayDribblingClass='Normal' AND SUBSTR(a.date,1,4)='2014' AND a.chanceCreationPassing<(SELECT CAST(SUM(b.chanceCreationPassing) AS REAL)/COUNT(u.id) FROM Team u JOIN Team_Attributes b ON u.team_api_id=b.team_api_id WHERE b.buildUpPlayDribblingClass='Normal' AND SUBSTR(b.date,1,4)='2014') ORDER BY a.chanceCreationPassing DESC
review_basis: Apply the question/evidence 2014 scope to the selected outer records as well as the population mean. Preserve qualifying-record multiplicity; do not silently add DISTINCT.

original_question: Please provide top five football players' IDs who are among the lowest potential players and prefer to use the right foot when attacking.
original_evidence: lowest potential players refers to MIN(potential); prefer to use the right foot when attacking refers to preferred_foot = 'right'
previous_SQLite: SELECT id FROM Player_Attributes WHERE preferred_foot = 'right' ORDER BY potential DESC LIMIT 5
accepted_SQLite: SELECT id FROM Player_Attributes WHERE preferred_foot = 'right' ORDER BY potential LIMIT 5
review_basis: Official revision changes DESC to ASC. Source domain check finds no NULL potential among preferred_foot=right, so NULL-first cannot select an unknown rating here.

original_question: How many of the patients with the most serious thrombosis cases examined in 1997 are women?
original_evidence: the most serious thrombosis refers to Thrombosis = '1' (the most severe one); women refers to sex = 'F'
previous_SQLite: SELECT  COUNT(*) FROM Patient AS T1 INNER JOIN Examination AS T2 ON T1.ID = T2.ID WHERE T1.SEX = 'F' AND STRFTIME('%Y', T2.`Examination Date`) = '1997' AND T2.Thrombosis = 1
accepted_SQLite: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) FROM Patient p JOIN Examination e ON p.ID=e.ID WHERE p.SEX='F' AND STRFTIME('%Y',e."Examination Date")='1997' AND e.Thrombosis=1
review_basis: Count patients, not potentially repeated examination events. On the shipped data both counts happen to be one; the entity-level distinction is explicit.

original_question: How many female patients born in 1964 were admitted to the hospital? List them by ID.
original_evidence: female refers to SEX = 'F'; born in 1964 refers to YEAR(Birthday) = 1964; admitted to the hospital refers to Admission = '+'
previous_SQLite: SELECT ID FROM Patient WHERE STRFTIME('%Y', Birthday) = '1964' AND SEX = 'F' AND Admission = '+'
accepted_SQLite: SELECT ID,COUNT(*) OVER() AS patient_count FROM Patient WHERE STRFTIME('%Y',Birthday)='1964' AND SEX='F' AND Admission='+' ORDER BY ID
review_basis: Return the requested patient IDs and their total count, with ID order explicit. The appended count column is an intentional, recorded output-contract revision.

original_question: What percentage of patients with a proteinuria level within the normal range have a uric acid level below the normal range?
original_evidence: proteinuria level within the normal range refers to `U-PRO` > 0 AND `U-PRO` < 30; uric acid level below the normal range refers to UA < = 6.5; calculation = MULTIPLY(DIVIDE(UA < = 6.5, `U-PRO` > 0 AND `U-PRO` < 30)，100)
previous_SQLite: SELECT CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN UA <= 6.5 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / COUNT(ID) FROM Laboratory WHERE `U-PRO` > 0 AND `U-PRO` < 30
accepted_SQLite: SELECT CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN UA <= 6.5 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / COUNT(ID) FROM Laboratory WHERE CAST(`U-PRO` AS REAL) > 0 AND CAST(`U-PRO` AS REAL) < 30
review_basis: Official correction casts U-PRO TEXT to REAL before >0/<30. Retain official SQLite numeric-prefix conversion for +1(30)/+2(100), rather than invent clinical values or compare text.

original_question: How many male patients who underwent testing between 1995 and 1997 and were subsequently diagnosed with Behcet disease did not stay in the hospital for treatment?
original_evidence: male refers to SEX = 'M'; underwent testing between 1995 and 1997 refers to `Examination Date` between '1995' and '1997'; Behcet refers to diagnosis; did not stay in the hospital refers to Admission = '-'
previous_SQLite: SELECT COUNT(T1.ID) FROM Patient AS T1 INNER JOIN Examination AS T2 ON T1.ID = T2.ID WHERE T2.Diagnosis = 'Behcet' AND T1.SEX = 'M' AND STRFTIME('%Y', T2.`Examination Date`) BETWEEN '1995' AND '1997' AND T1.Admission = '-'
accepted_SQLite: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) FROM Patient p JOIN Examination e ON p.ID=e.ID WHERE e.Diagnosis='Behcet' AND p.SEX='M' AND STRFTIME('%Y',e."Examination Date") BETWEEN '1995' AND '1997' AND p.Admission='-'
review_basis: Count distinct male patients, rather than repeated examinations. Preserve exact case-sensitive Examination.Diagnosis=Behcet; the observed domain has this spelling.

original_question: Please provide the diagnosis of patients with ALT glutamic pylvic transaminase beyond the normal range by ascending order of their date of birth.
original_evidence: ALT glutamic pylvic transaminase beyond the normal range refers to GPT > 60; The larger the birthday value, the younger the person is, and vice versa;
previous_SQLite: SELECT DISTINCT T1.Diagnosis FROM Patient AS T1 INNER JOIN Laboratory AS T2 ON T1.ID = T2.ID WHERE T2.GPT > 60 ORDER BY T1.Birthday ASC
accepted_SQLite: WITH eligible AS (SELECT p.ID,p.Diagnosis,p.Birthday,ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY p.Diagnosis ORDER BY p.Birthday ASC,p.ID ASC) AS rn FROM Patient p WHERE EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory l WHERE l.ID=p.ID AND l.GPT>60)) SELECT Diagnosis FROM eligible WHERE rn=1 ORDER BY Birthday ASC,ID ASC
review_basis: The official DISTINCT diagnosis with hidden Birthday order does not define a birthday for repeated diagnoses. This reference explicitly chooses the earliest eligible birthday (NULL first) per diagnosis, then orders those representatives. It is a documented clarification, not a universal-equivalence claim for the old hidden-key SQL.

original_question: List the patient ID, sex and birthday who has abnormal white blood cell count. Group them by sex and list the patient by age in ascending order.
original_evidence: abnormal white blood cell count refers to WBC < = 3.5 or WBC > = 9.0;
previous_SQLite: SELECT DISTINCT T1.ID, T1.SEX, T1.Birthday FROM Patient AS T1 INNER JOIN Laboratory AS T2 ON T1.ID = T2.ID WHERE T2.WBC <= 3.5 OR T2.WBC >= 9.0 GROUP BY T1.SEX,T1.ID ORDER BY T1.Birthday ASC
accepted_SQLite: SELECT p.ID,p.SEX,p.Birthday FROM Patient p WHERE EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory l WHERE l.ID=p.ID AND (l.WBC<=3.5 OR l.WBC>=9.0)) ORDER BY p.SEX ASC,p.Birthday DESC
review_basis: Keep original inclusive WBC thresholds. Order sex groups and then ascending age (Birthday DESC); use unique Patient.ID to avoid multiplying patients by lab records.

original_question: For all patients who are older than 55 years old, what is the percentage of female who has abnormal prothrombin time (PT)?
original_evidence: older than 55 years old = SUBTRACT(year(current_timestamp), year(Birthday)) > 55; abnormal prothrombin time (PT) refers to PT > = 14; percentage = DIVIDE(SUM(PT > = 14 AND SEX = 'F'), SUM(PT > = 14)) * 100; female refers to sex = 'F';
previous_SQLite: SELECT CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN T2.PT >= 14 AND T1.SEX = 'F' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / COUNT(*) FROM Patient AS T1 INNER JOIN Laboratory AS T2 ON T1.ID = T2.ID WHERE STRFTIME('%Y', CURRENT_TIMESTAMP) - STRFTIME('%Y', T1.Birthday) > 55
accepted_SQLite:
SELECT 
    CAST(COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN T2.PT >= 14 AND T1.SEX = 'F' THEN T1.ID END) AS REAL)
    / COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN T2.PT >= 14 THEN T1.ID END)
    * 100 AS abnormal_pt_female_percentage
FROM Patient AS T1
INNER JOIN Laboratory AS T2 ON T1.ID = T2.ID
WHERE STRFTIME('%Y', CURRENT_TIMESTAMP) - STRFTIME('%Y', T1.Birthday) > 55;
review_basis: Official correction divides distinct older female abnormal-PT patients by distinct older abnormal-PT patients; do not restore the old all-patients denominator.

original_question: Please list the ID of the patient whose RF is normal and who is older than 60.
original_evidence: RF is normal refers to RF < 20; older than 60 = SUBTRACT((YEAR(CURDATE()), YEAR(Birthday))) > 60;
previous_SQLite: SELECT T1.ID FROM Patient AS T1 INNER JOIN Laboratory AS T2 ON T1.ID = T2.ID WHERE T2.RF < 20 AND STRFTIME('%Y', DATE('now')) - STRFTIME('%Y', T1.Birthday) > 60
accepted_SQLite: SELECT p.ID FROM Patient p JOIN Laboratory l ON p.ID=l.ID WHERE l.RF IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(l.RF)!='' AND CAST(REPLACE(REPLACE(l.RF,'<',''),'>','') AS REAL)<20 AND CAST(STRFTIME('%Y',DATE('now')) AS INTEGER)-CAST(STRFTIME('%Y',p.Birthday) AS INTEGER)>60
review_basis: Apply the user-approved official RF sign-removal comparison, with recorded censored-measurement limitations. Preserve original current-year age and join multiplicity; do not substitute age at laboratory test.

original_question: How many patients with a normal RF don't have thrombosis?
original_evidence: normal RF refers to RF < 20; don't have thrombosis refers to Thrombosis = '0';
previous_SQLite: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT T1.ID) FROM Examination AS T1 INNER JOIN Laboratory AS T2 ON T1.ID = T2.ID WHERE T2.RF < 20 AND T1.Thrombosis = 0
accepted_SQLite: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT e.ID) FROM Examination e JOIN Laboratory l ON e.ID=l.ID WHERE l.RF IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(l.RF)!='' AND CAST(REPLACE(REPLACE(l.RF,'<',''),'>','') AS REAL)<20 AND e.Thrombosis=0
review_basis: Apply the same user-approved RF sign-removal policy as q1260; original/latest RF TEXT<20 comparison is lexical. Preserve distinct patient count and Thrombosis=0.

original_question: For the patients who have an abnormal level of anti-DNA, please list the diseases they are diagnosed with.
original_evidence: abnormal level of anti-DNA refers to DNA > = 8; diseases refers to Diagnosis;
previous_SQLite: SELECT DISTINCT(T1.Diagnosis) FROM Patient AS T1 INNER JOIN Laboratory AS T2 ON T1.ID = T2.ID WHERE T2.DNA >= 8
accepted_SQLite: SELECT DISTINCT p.Diagnosis FROM Patient p JOIN Laboratory l ON p.ID=l.ID WHERE CAST(l.DNA AS REAL)>=8
review_basis: Original/latest SQLite DNA column has TEXT affinity and compares decimal strings lexically. Evidence requires numeric anti-DNA threshold 8. All 66 distinct non-NULL DNA values are valid decimal numbers; explicit REAL cast preserves NULL and requested diagnosis/patient multiplicity.

original_question: How many patients have a normal anti-DNA level, yet their data are not recorded.
original_evidence: normal anti-DNA level refers to DNA < 8; data are not recorded refers to Description IS NULL; Should compute the number of unique ones
previous_SQLite: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT T1.ID) FROM Patient AS T1 INNER JOIN Laboratory AS T2 ON T1.ID = T2.ID WHERE T2.DNA < 8 AND T1.Description IS NULL
accepted_SQLite: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) FROM Patient p JOIN Laboratory l ON p.ID=l.ID WHERE CAST(l.DNA AS REAL)<8 AND p.Description IS NULL
review_basis: Original/latest SQLite DNA column has TEXT affinity and compares decimal strings lexically. Evidence requires numeric anti-DNA threshold 8. All 66 distinct non-NULL DNA values are valid decimal numbers; explicit REAL cast preserves NULL and requested diagnosis/patient multiplicity.

original_question: Please list the top three patients' birthdays with the highest glutamic pylvic transaminase in the normal range.
original_evidence: highest glutamic pylvic transaminase in the normal range refers to MAX(GPT < 60);
previous_SQLite: SELECT T1.Birthday FROM Patient AS T1 INNER JOIN Laboratory AS T2 ON T1.ID = T2.ID WHERE T2.GPT < 60 ORDER BY T2.GPT DESC LIMIT 3
accepted_SQLite: SELECT T1.Birthday FROM Patient AS T1 INNER JOIN Laboratory AS T2 ON T1.ID = T2.ID WHERE T2.GPT < 60 GROUP BY T1.ID ORDER BY MAX(T2.GPT) DESC, T1.ID ASC LIMIT 3
review_basis: Official correction groups by patient ID, ranks MAX(GPT) below 60 and uses ID tie breaking. Include Birthday in Oracle GROUP BY using the verified ID dependency.

original_question: Please list a patient's platelet level if it is within the normal range and if he or she is diagnosed with MCTD.
original_evidence: PLT > 100 and PLT < 400 means platelet level is within the normal range; PLT < 100 and PLT > 400 means platelet level is not within the normal range; diagnosed with MCTD refers to Diagnosis = 'MCTD';
previous_SQLite: SELECT T2.PLT FROM Patient AS T1 INNER JOIN Laboratory AS T2 ON T1.ID = T2.ID WHERE T1.Diagnosis = 'MCTD' AND T2.PLT BETWEEN 100 AND 400
accepted_SQLite: SELECT l.PLT FROM Patient p JOIN Laboratory l ON p.ID=l.ID WHERE p.Diagnosis='MCTD' AND l.PLT>100 AND l.PLT<400
review_basis: Evidence defines the normal platelet interval as open. Change only >100/<400 and retain the independent, unknown historical paid-request state; no model request is sent.

original_question: List the full name of the top five members who spend the most money in the descending order of spending.
original_evidence: full name refers to first_name, last_name; spend the most money refers to MAX(expense.cost)
previous_SQLite: SELECT T3.first_name, T3.last_name FROM expense AS T1 INNER JOIN budget AS T2 ON T1.link_to_budget = T2.budget_id INNER JOIN member AS T3 ON T1.link_to_member = T3.member_id ORDER BY T2.spent DESC LIMIT 5
accepted_SQLite: SELECT T2.first_name, T2.last_name FROM expense AS T1 INNER JOIN member AS T2 ON T1.link_to_member = T2.member_id GROUP BY T2.member_id, T2.first_name, T2.last_name ORDER BY SUM(T1.cost) DESC LIMIT 5
review_basis: Official correction removes the budget join and ranks each member by SUM(expense.cost); preserve names and member grouping.
